title.zh: 卷505 列傳二百九十二 艺術四
title.raw: 卷505 列傳二百九十二 艺術四

sentences.zh: 王來咸褚士寶馮行貞甘鳳池曹竹齋潘佩言

translations.literal: Wang Laixian, Chu Shibao, Feng Xingzhen, Gan Fengchi, Cao Zhuzhai, Pan Peiyan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Laixian, Chu Shibao, Feng Xingzhen, Gan Fengchi, Cao Zhuzhai, and Pan Peiyan

sentences.zh: 江之桐梁九張漣葉陶劉源唐英戴梓

translations.literal: Jiang Zhitong, Liang Jiu, Zhang Lian, Ye Tao, Liu Yuan, Tang Ying, Dai Zi
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhitong, Liang Jiu, Zhang Lian, Ye Tao, Liu Yuan, Tang Ying, and Dai Zi

sentences.zh: 丁守存徐壽子建寅華封

translations.literal: Ding Shoucun, Xu Shou, Zi Jianyin, Hua Feng
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shoucun, Xu Shou, Zi Jianyin, and Hua Feng

sentences.zh: 王來咸，字征南，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Laixian, style name Zhengnan, was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Laixian, whose style was Zhengnan, came from Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 先世居奉化，自祖父居鄞，至來咸徙同，從同里單思南受內家拳法。

translations.literal: His forebears had lived in Fenghua; from his grandfather's generation the family resided in Yin, and by Laixian's time they moved to Tongqiu, where he received the internal-school boxing method from Shan Sinan, a man of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: The family had originally lived in Fenghua, but his grandfather settled in Yin, and Laixian later moved to Tongqiu and studied internal-school boxing under his fellow townsman Shan Sinan.

sentences.zh: 內家者，起於宋武當道士張三峰，其法以靜制動，應手即僕，與少林之主於搏人者異，故別少林為外家。

translations.literal: The internal school arose with the Song-dynasty Wudang Daoist Zhang Sanfeng; its method uses stillness to overcome movement, and an opponent falls as soon as one meets his attack. It differs from Shaolin, which chiefly relies on grappling and striking down others, and so Shaolin is set apart as the external school.
translations.idiomatic: The internal school traces back to the Wudang Daoist Zhang Sanfeng of the Song. Its art subdues motion through stillness, and attackers fall the moment one engages them. Because this differs from Shaolin's emphasis on overpowering an opponent by force, Shaolin is treated as the external school.

sentences.zh: 其後流傳於秦、晉間，至明中葉，王宗岳為最著，溫州、陳州同受之，遂流傳於溫州。

translations.literal: Later it spread through the Qin and Jin regions; by the mid-Ming, Wang Zongyue was the most celebrated master. Wenzhou and Chenzhou alike received the transmission, and the art then spread in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The art later circulated through Qin and Jin. In the mid-Ming, Wang Zongyue became its most famous exponent; both Wenzhou and Chenzhou received the tradition, after which it flourished in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，張松溪最著，松溪之徒三四人，寧波葉繼美為魁，遂流傳於寧波。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign, Zhang Songxi was the most renowned; Songxi had three or four disciples, among whom Ye Jimei of Ningbo was foremost, and the art then spread in Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era Zhang Songxi stood at the height of fame. He had three or four disciples, with Ye Jimei of Ningbo as their leader, and the tradition thereafter took root in Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 得繼美之傳者，曰吳崑山、周雲泉、陳貞石、孫繼槎及思南，各有授受。

translations.literal: Those who received Jimei's transmission were Wu Kunshan, Zhou Yunquan, Chen Zhenshi, Sun Jiqiao, and Sinan, each with his own line of master and pupil.
translations.idiomatic: Jimei's disciples included Wu Kunshan, Zhou Yunquan, Chen Zhenshi, Sun Jiqiao, and Sinan, each maintaining a separate teaching line.

sentences.zh: 思南從征關白，歸老於家，以術教，頗惜其精微。

translations.literal: Sinan followed the campaign against Konose, retired at home in old age, and taught the art, yet was quite reluctant to reveal its finest subtleties.
translations.idiomatic: Sinan had served in the campaign against Konose, and in retirement he taught the art but was reluctant to pass on its most refined secrets.

sentences.zh: 來咸從樓上穴板窺之，得其梗概。

translations.literal: Laixian bored through the floorboards from upstairs to spy on him and grasped the general outline of the method.
translations.idiomatic: Laixian drilled holes in the floor above and watched the lessons, learning the art in outline.

sentences.zh: 以銀卮易美檟奉思南，始盡以不傳者傳之。

translations.literal: He exchanged a silver goblet for a fine coffin and presented it to Sinan, whereupon Sinan at last transmitted to him everything he had withheld.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Sinan a silver cup in exchange for a fine coffin as a gift, and only then did Sinan teach him everything he had previously withheld.

sentences.zh: 來咸為人機警，不露圭角，非遇甚困不發。

translations.literal: Laixian was quick-witted by nature, never showing a sharp edge, and would not unleash his skill unless driven to great straits.
translations.idiomatic: Laixian was sharp and alert by nature, kept his abilities hidden, and would not use his art unless he was pushed to the limit.

sentences.zh: 凡搏人皆以其穴，死穴、暈穴、啞穴，一切如銅人圖法。

translations.literal: Whenever he struck down an opponent he targeted the acupoints—death points, fainting points, and mute points—all according to the method shown on the bronze-man diagram.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight he struck the vital points—death points, fainting points, and mute points—exactly as prescribed on the bronze acupoint manikin.

sentences.zh: 有惡少侮之，為所擊，數日不溺，謝過，乃得如故。

translations.literal: A vicious youth insulted him and was struck; for several days he could not urinate, but after apologizing he recovered as before.
translations.idiomatic: When a bully harassed him, Laixian struck him in a vital point, and the man could not urinate for days until he apologized, after which he returned to normal.

sentences.zh: 牧童竊學其法，擊伴侶，立死。

translations.literal: A herd boy secretly learned his method, struck a companion, and the companion died on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: A shepherd boy who had secretly picked up the technique struck a playmate, who collapsed and died at once.

sentences.zh: 視之，曰：「此暈穴。

translations.literal: Laixian looked and said, "This is a fainting point.
translations.idiomatic: Laixian examined him and said, "That was a fainting point.

sentences.zh: 」不久果甦。

translations.literal: " Before long the boy indeed revived.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the boy did revive.

sentences.zh: 任俠，嘗為人報仇，有致金以讎其弟者，絕之，曰：「此以禽獸待我也！

translations.literal: He was chivalrous and once avenged others; when someone offered him gold to settle a score against that man's younger brother, he refused and said, "You are treating me like a beast!
translations.idiomatic: A man of chivalry, he sometimes took revenge for others; once someone offered him gold to kill the man's younger brother, but he refused, saying, "You treat me like an animal!

sentences.zh: 」明末，嘗入伍為把總，從錢肅樂起兵浙東，事敗，隱居於家。

translations.literal: " At the end of the Ming he once entered the ranks as a platoon commander, followed Qian Sule in raising troops in eastern Zhejiang, and when the cause failed he lived in seclusion at home.
translations.idiomatic: " In the late Ming he enlisted as a platoon commander and joined Qian Sule's uprising in eastern Zhejiang; when the effort collapsed he withdrew into private life.

sentences.zh: 慕其藝者，多通殷勤，皆不顧。

translations.literal: Many who admired his art sent him tokens of regard, but he paid no attention to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who admired his skill often sent him gifts and courtesies, but he ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 鋤地擔糞，安於食貧。

translations.literal: He hoed fields and carried night soil, content to live in poverty.
translations.idiomatic: He hoed the earth and carried manure, content with a poor man's fare.

sentences.zh: 未嘗讀書，與士大夫談論蘊藉，不知為粗人。

translations.literal: He had never studied books, yet in conversation with scholar-officials he was refined and restrained, and one would not know he was a rough man.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had never studied the classics, his talk with scholar-officials was cultivated and restrained, and no one would have taken him for a coarse fellow.

sentences.zh: 黃宗羲與之遊，同入天童，僧少焰有膂力，四五人不能掣其手，稍近來咸，蹶然負痛。

translations.literal: Huang Zongxi associated with him and once entered Tiantong Monastery with him; the monk Shaoyan had great strength, and four or five men could not pull his hand away, but when he drew slightly near Laixian he suddenly collapsed in pain.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi befriended him and once visited Tiantong Monastery with him. The monk Shaoyan was immensely strong—four or five men together could not break his grip—but when he came near Laixian he suddenly crumpled in pain.

sentences.zh: 來咸嘗曰：「今人以內家無可炫耀，於是以外家羼之，此學行衰矣！

translations.literal: Laixian once said, "Nowadays people find nothing in the internal school worth showing off, so they mix in the external school—this is how the art has declined!
translations.idiomatic: Laixian once remarked, "People today find the internal school too subtle to show off, so they blend in external-school techniques—that is why the tradition is in decline!

sentences.zh: 」因為宗羲論述其學源流。

translations.literal: " He therefore expounded to Zongxi the origins and transmission of his school.
translations.idiomatic: " He then laid out for Zongxi the lineage and sources of the art.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of the Kangxi reign, at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 宗羲子百家從之學，演其說為內家拳法一卷，百家後無所傳焉。

translations.literal: Zongxi's son Baijia studied under him and developed his teachings into one fascicle on Internal-School Boxing; afterward Baijia had no one to whom he transmitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxi's son Baijia studied under him and set out his teachings in a single fascicle entitled Internal-School Boxing, but Baijia later left no successor.

sentences.zh: 清中葉，河北有太極拳，云其法出於山西王宗岳，其法式論解，與百家之言相出入。

translations.literal: In the mid-Qing, Hebei had Taiji boxing, said to derive from Wang Zongyue of Shanxi; its forms, treatises, and explanations diverged somewhat from Baijia's account.
translations.idiomatic: By the mid-Qing, Taiji boxing had appeared in Hebei, traditionally traced to Wang Zongyue of Shanxi; its forms and theoretical writings differed in places from what Baijia had recorded.

sentences.zh: 至清末，傳習者頗眾雲。

translations.literal: By the late Qing those who practiced and transmitted it were quite numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Qing a great many people were practicing and teaching it.

sentences.zh: 褚士寶，字復生，江南上海人。

translations.literal: Chu Shibao, style name Fusheng, was a native of Shanghai in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Shibao, whose style was Fusheng, came from Shanghai in the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 家素封，膂力過人，好技擊，遊學四方。

translations.literal: His family had long been wealthy; his physical strength surpassed others', he delighted in martial arts, and he traveled to study in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Born into a wealthy household, he possessed extraordinary strength, loved the martial arts, and wandered far and wide to study them.

sentences.zh: 與畢昆陽、武君卿為友，遂精槍法，名曰四平槍，旋轉如風，人莫能近。

translations.literal: He befriended Bi Kunyang and Wu Junqing and thereby mastered spear technique, called the Four-Level Spear; it spun like the wind and no one could come near him.
translations.idiomatic: Through his friendship with Bi Kunyang and Wu Junqing he mastered spear fighting, known as the Four-Level Spear—its whirl was like wind, and no opponent could close on him.

sentences.zh: 同邑有張擎者，虎頸板肋，力舉百鈞，橫行為閭里患，眾請士寶除之。

translations.literal: In the same district there was a Zhang Qing, bull-necked and slab-ribbed, able to lift a hundred jun; he rampaged through the neighborhood and became a scourge, and the people asked Shibao to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman named Zhang Qing had a bull neck and barrel chest and could lift enormous weights; his bullying made him a neighborhood menace, and the community begged Shibao to deal with him.

sentences.zh: 同飲酒，擎自誇其勇，酒酣，攘臂作勢，士寶徐以箸點其胸，曰：「子盍坐而言乎？

translations.literal: They drank together; Qing boasted of his bravery, and when the wine was deep he rolled up his sleeves and struck a pose. Shibao slowly touched his chest with chopsticks and said, "Why not sit down and speak calmly?
translations.idiomatic: They shared a drinking bout. Qing bragged about his prowess, and when he was drunk he rolled up his sleeves threateningly. Shibao gently tapped his chest with his chopsticks and said, "Why don't you sit down and talk this over?

sentences.zh: 」擎遂默然，少頃辭去，越日，死於橋亭。

translations.literal: " Qing then fell silent; shortly he took his leave, and the next day he died at the bridge pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing fell silent, left shortly afterward, and was found dead the next day at the bridge pavilion.

sentences.zh: 明季福王南渡，兵部員外郎何剛薦士寶為伏波營游擊。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu crossed south in the late Ming, He Gang, an assistant secretary in the Ministry of War, recommended Shibao as mobile-detachment commander of the Fubo Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, when the Prince of Fu fled south, He Gang of the Ministry of War recommended Shibao for the post of mobile-detachment commander in the Fubo Camp.

sentences.zh: 未之官，南​​都陷，終老於家。

translations.literal: Before he took office the Southern Capital fell, and he ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: He never assumed the post; Nanjing fell, and he lived out his life at home.

sentences.zh: 所傳弟子有王聖蕃、池天榮。

translations.literal: Among the disciples to whom he transmitted the art were Wang Shengfan and Chi Tianrong.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples included Wang Shengfan and Chi Tianrong.

sentences.zh: 天榮又傳浙江提督喬照。

translations.literal: Tianrong in turn transmitted it to Qiao Zhao, provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianrong passed the art on to Qiao Zhao, the Zhejiang provincial commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其槍譜二種及治傷藥酒方，世猶有藏之者。

translations.literal: His two spear manuals and his medicinal wine formulas for treating wounds are still preserved by some in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Two of his spear manuals and his recipes for medicinal wines to treat wounds are still kept in private collections.

sentences.zh: 馮行貞，字服之，江南常熟人。

translations.literal: Feng Xingzhen, style name Fuzhi, was a native of Changshu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingzhen, whose style was Fuzhi, came from Changshu in the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 父班，以文學者。

translations.literal: His father Ban was known for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ban was a scholar of letters.

sentences.zh: 兄行賢，傳其學。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xingxian inherited his father's learning.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xingxian carried on their father's scholarship.

sentences.zh: 行貞少亦喜讀書，工小詞，性倜儻不羈。

translations.literal: Xingzhen in youth also loved reading, was skilled at short lyrics, and by nature was free-spirited and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Xingzhen also loved books, wrote polished short lyrics, and had a bold, unconstrained temperament.

sentences.zh: 善射，能以後矢落前矢，投石子於百步外無不中。

translations.literal: He excelled at archery and could knock down the leading arrow with a following one; he hurled stones a hundred paces and never missed.
translations.idiomatic: He was a superb archer who could split one arrow in flight with the next, and at a hundred paces his thrown stones never missed their mark.

sentences.zh: 實雞卵殼以礦灰，遇劇盜，輒先發雞卵中其目。

translations.literal: He filled eggshells with mineral lime; when he met fierce bandits he would first launch the eggs and strike their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: He packed eggshells with powdered lime and, when confronted by violent robbers, would hurl them first to blind his foes.

sentences.zh: 山東響馬老瓜賊為行旅患，聞馮氏名，莫敢攖。

translations.literal: The mounted bandits called Old Melon Thieves in Shandong were a scourge to travelers, but hearing the Feng family's name none dared provoke them.
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong mounted bandits known as the Old Melon Thieves terrorized travelers, yet once they heard the Feng name they dared not molest them.

sentences.zh: 從休寧程打虎及張老受槍法，馳突無敵。

translations.literal: He studied spear technique under Cheng Dahu of Xiuning and Old Zhang, and in sudden charges he was without rival.
translations.idiomatic: Under Cheng Dahu of Xiuning and Old Zhang he mastered the spear and was unmatched in the charge.

sentences.zh: 山行遇虎，以短槍斃之。

translations.literal: Once while traveling in the mountains he met a tiger and killed it with a short spear.
translations.idiomatic: While crossing the mountains he once met a tiger and brought it down with a short spear.

sentences.zh: 嘗為客報仇。

translations.literal: He once avenged a client.
translations.idiomatic: He once took revenge on behalf of a patron.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，從康親王杰書軍南征，有功，當得官，尋棄歸。

translations.literal: During Kangxi he followed Prince Kang Jieshu's army on the southern campaign, performed meritorious service, and was due to receive an office, but soon abandoned his post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi reign he served under Prince Kang Jieshu in the southern campaigns, earned distinction, and was offered an official post, but soon resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 僑居吳中婁門外村落，以經書教授，詩畫自娛。

translations.literal: He lived as a sojourner in a village outside Lou Gate in Wu, taught the classics, and amused himself with poetry and painting.
translations.idiomatic: He settled in a village beyond Lou Gate in Wu, taught the classics for a living, and passed his days in poetry and painting.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，卒。

translations.literal: He died in his seventies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 以槍法授同縣陶元淳，元淳後無傳者。

translations.literal: He transmitted his spear method to Tao Yuanchun of the same county, but afterward Yuanchun had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: He taught his spear art to Tao Yuanchun of his home county, but Yuanchun left no heir to the tradition.

sentences.zh: 甘鳳池，江南江寧人。

translations.literal: Gan Fengchi was a native of Jiangning in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Fengchi came from Jiangning in the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 少以勇聞。

translations.literal: From youth he was famed for courage.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for bravery from an early age.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，客京師貴邸。

translations.literal: During Kangxi he lodged as a guest in the mansions of the nobility in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he was a guest in the households of great families in the capital.

sentences.zh: 力士張大義者慕其名，自濟南來見。

translations.literal: A strongman named Zhang Dayi, admiring his reputation, came from Jinan to see him.
translations.idiomatic: A wrestler named Zhang Dayi, who admired his fame, traveled from Jinan to meet him.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，命與鳳池角，鳳池辭，固強之。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep they ordered him to wrestle with Fengchi; Fengchi declined, but they pressed him firmly.
translations.idiomatic: After much wine they insisted he wrestle Fengchi; Fengchi refused, but they would not let him decline.

sentences.zh: 大義身長八尺餘，脛力強大，以鐵裹拇，騰躍若風雨之驟至。

translations.literal: Dayi stood more than eight chi tall, with powerful shins; he wrapped his thumbs in iron and leaped like a sudden storm.
translations.idiomatic: Dayi stood over eight feet tall, with tremendous leg strength; he bound iron around his thumbs and sprang about like a sudden squall.

sentences.zh: 鳳池卻立倚柱，俟其來，承以手，大義大呼僕，血滿鞾，解視，拇盡嵌鐵中。

translations.literal: Fengchi stepped back and stood leaning on a pillar, waited for him to come, and received him with his hand; Dayi cried out and fell, blood filling his boots; when they unwrapped him, both thumbs were embedded in the iron.
translations.idiomatic: Fengchi drew back against a pillar, waited for the charge, and caught him with his hand. Dayi shouted and collapsed, blood soaking his boots; when they unwrapped his thumbs, both were driven into the iron bindings.

sentences.zh: 即墨馬玉麟，長軀大腹，以帛約身，緣牆升木，捷於猱。

translations.literal: Ma Yulin of Jimo had a long frame and great belly; he bound his body with cloth, scaled walls and climbed trees, and was swifter than a monkey.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yulin of Jimo was tall and broad-bellied; swathed in cloth strips, he could run up walls and trees faster than a monkey.

sentences.zh: 客揚州巨賈家，鳳池後至，居其上。

translations.literal: He was a guest in the house of a great merchant in Yangzhou; Fengchi arrived later and was lodged above him.
translations.idiomatic: He was staying with a wealthy Yangzhou merchant when Fengchi arrived afterward and was given the better quarters upstairs.

sentences.zh: 玉麟不平，與角技，終日無勝負。

translations.literal: Yulin took offense and wrestled with him; all day long neither could win.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin resented the slight and challenged him to a match; they wrestled all day without a decision.

sentences.zh: 鳳池曰：「此勁敵，非張大義比！

translations.literal: Fengchi said, "This is a formidable foe—not to be compared with Zhang Dayi!
translations.idiomatic: Fengchi said, "Here is a real opponent—not in Zhang Dayi's class!

sentences.zh: 」明日又角，數蹈其瑕，玉麟直前擒鳳池，以駢指卻之，玉麟僕地，慚遁。

translations.literal: " The next day they wrestled again; several times Fengchi exploited his flaws. Yulin rushed forward to seize Fengchi, but Fengchi repelled him with joined fingers; Yulin fell to the ground and fled in shame.
translations.idiomatic: " They wrestled again the next day. Fengchi repeatedly found openings; Yulin lunged to grab him, but Fengchi drove him back with a two-finger strike. Yulin fell and slunk away in humiliation.

sentences.zh: 鳳池嘗語人曰：「吾力不逾中人，所以能勝人者，善藉其力以製之耳。

translations.literal: Fengchi once told others, "My strength does not exceed that of an ordinary man; the reason I can overcome others is that I am skilled at borrowing their force to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Fengchi once said, "My strength is no greater than an average man's. I win because I know how to borrow an opponent's force and turn it against him.

sentences.zh: 」手能破堅，握鉛錫化為水。

translations.literal: " His hands could break what was hard; when he grasped lead and tin they melted like water.
translations.idiomatic: " His grip could shatter hard objects, and when he closed his hand on lead or tin they melted as if they were water.

sentences.zh: 又善導引術，同里譚氏子病瘵，醫不效，鳳池於靜室窒牖戶，夜與合背坐，四十九日而痊。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in daoyin exercises; a son of the Tan family in his district suffered from consumption and medicine failed. Fengchi sealed the windows in a quiet room, sat back to back with him at night, and after forty-nine days he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He was also adept at daoyin breathing exercises. When a neighbor's son in the Tan clan fell ill with consumption and doctors could not cure him, Fengchi sealed a quiet room and sat back to back with the boy each night; after forty-nine days the youth recovered.

sentences.zh: 喜任俠，接人和易，見者不知為賁、育。

translations.literal: He delighted in chivalry and received people with easy grace; those who met him did not know he was another Benke or Yuji.
translations.idiomatic: He loved acts of chivalry and treated everyone with easy warmth; strangers meeting him would never have guessed he was a man of Herculean strength.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，浙江總督李衛捕治江寧顧云如邪術不軌獄，株連百數十人，鳳池亦被逮，讞擬大辟。

translations.literal: During Yongzheng, Li Wei, governor-general of Zhejiang, arrested and tried the Jiangning case of Gu Yunru's heterodox arts and sedition, implicating several hundred people; Fengchi was also seized, and the verdict proposed the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng reign, Zhejiang governor-general Li Wei prosecuted the Jiangning case of Gu Yunru's sorcery and sedition, implicating scores of people. Fengchi was arrested as well, and the sentence called for execution.

sentences.zh: 世宗於此獄從寬，未盡駢誅。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor showed leniency in this case and did not carry out mass joint execution.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor showed mercy in the affair, and not all those implicated were executed together.

sentences.zh: 或云鳳池年八十餘，終於家。

translations.literal: Some say Fengchi lived to more than eighty and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Some accounts say Fengchi lived past eighty and died at home.

sentences.zh: 江湖間流傳其佚事多荒誕，著其可信者。

translations.literal: Among the rivers and lakes many wild tales about him circulate, most of them fantastic; here only what is credible is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Countless fanciful stories about him circulate in popular lore; only those that seem credible are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 曹竹齋，以字行，佚其名，福建人。

translations.literal: Cao Zhuzhai was known by his style name; his personal name is lost. He was a native of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhuzhai was known only by his style; his given name is unrecorded. He came from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 老而貧，賣卜揚州市。

translations.literal: In old age he was poor and practiced divination for sale in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He grew old in poverty and earned his living telling fortunes in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 江、淮間健者，莫能當其一拳，故稱曹一拳。

translations.literal: Among the strong men between the Yangtze and Huai, none could withstand a single punch of his, and so he was called Cao One-Fist.
translations.idiomatic: No brawler along the Yangtze and Huai could withstand a single blow from him, and he was known as Cao One-Fist.

sentences.zh: 少年以重幣請其術，不可。

translations.literal: Young men offered heavy payment to learn his art, but he would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Young men offered him large sums to teach his art, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 或怪之，則曰：「此皆無賴子，豈當授藝以助虐哉？

translations.literal: When some wondered at this, he said, "These are all ruffians—how could one teach them the art to help them tyrannize others?
translations.idiomatic: When people questioned him, he replied, "They are all good-for-nothings. Why should I teach them skills that would only help them bully others?

sentences.zh: 拳棒，古先舞蹈之遺也，君子習之，所以調血脈，養壽命，其粗乃以御侮。

translations.literal: Fist and staff are the legacy of the ancient ritual dances; the gentleman practices them to regulate the blood and vessels and nurture long life; only in their rough form are they used to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing and staff work descend from the ritual dances of antiquity. A gentleman practices them to harmonize the circulation and prolong life; only in their cruder application are they meant for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 必彼侮而我御之，若以之侮人，則反為人所禦而自敗矣。

translations.literal: One must wait until the other insults and then repel him; if one uses the art to insult others, one is instead repelled by others and defeats oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The art is for when others provoke you, not for provoking them; use it to bully others and they will turn it against you and you will bring about your own ruin.

sentences.zh: 無賴子以血氣事侵凌，其氣浮於上，而立腳虛，故因其奔赴之勢，略藉手而僕耳。

translations.literal: Ruffians rely on hot blood to bully others; their qi floats upward and their footing is empty, so one borrows the force of their rush and with a slight touch of the hand makes them fall.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffians attack in a surge of brute courage; their energy rides high and their stance is hollow. One need only borrow the momentum of their charge and with a light touch send them sprawling.

sentences.zh: 一身止兩拳，拳之大才數寸，焉足衛五尺之軀，且以接四面乎？

translations.literal: The body has only two fists, and each fist is but a few inches across—how could that suffice to guard a five-foot frame and meet attacks from all four sides?
translations.idiomatic: A man has only two fists, each a few inches wide—how could they alone defend a five-foot body against threats from every direction?

sentences.zh: 惟養吾正氣，使周於吾身，彼之手足近吾身，而吾之拳，即在其所近之處。

translations.literal: Only by nurturing one's upright qi so that it pervades the body—when the opponent's hands and feet approach one's body, one's fist is already where they approach.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivate your upright qi until it fills the whole body; then wherever an opponent's limbs come near you, your fist is already there to meet them.

sentences.zh: 以彼虛囂之氣，與吾靜定之氣接，則自無幸矣。

translations.literal: When their empty, clamorous qi meets our calm, settled qi, they naturally have no chance of success.
translations.idiomatic: When their hollow, blustering force meets your calm, grounded presence, they cannot prevail.

sentences.zh: 故至精是術者，其徵有二：一則精神貫注，而腹背皆乾滑如臘肉；

translations.literal: Therefore the master of this art to the highest degree shows two signs: first, his spirit is fully concentrated and his belly and back are dry and smooth like cured meat;
translations.idiomatic: The consummate practitioner shows two signs: first, his spirit is wholly focused and his belly and back are dry and smooth as cured meat;

sentences.zh: 一則氣體健舉，而額顱皆肥澤如粉粢。

translations.literal: second, his vital breath is robust and lifted, and his forehead and skull are plump and lustrous like powdered millet cakes.
translations.idiomatic: second, his breath is vigorous and lifted, and his brow and crown are full and lustrous like fresh rice cakes.

sentences.zh: 是皆血脈流行，應乎自然，內充實而外和平，犯而不校者也。

translations.literal: These all show the blood and vessels flowing in response to nature—full within and peaceful without, one who is wronged yet does not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Both show the blood circulating in harmony with nature—inwardly full, outwardly serene, the man who is provoked yet does not strike back in anger.

sentences.zh: 」嘉慶末，歿於揚州，年八十餘。

translations.literal: " At the end of the Jiaqing reign he died in Yangzhou, aged more than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in Yangzhou toward the end of the Jiaqing reign, aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 潘佩言，亦以字行，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Pan Peiyan, likewise known by his style name, was a native of She County, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Peiyan, also known by his style name, came from She County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以槍法著稱，稱潘五先生。

translations.literal: He was famed for spear technique and was called Master Pan the Fifth.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for his spear art and was known as Master Pan the Fifth.

sentences.zh: 其言：「槍長九尺，而桿圓四五寸，然槍入手，則全身悉委於桿。

translations.literal: He said, "The spear is nine chi long and the shaft is four or five inches round, yet once the spear is in the hand the whole body is entrusted to the shaft.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "A spear is nine feet long and the shaft four or five inches thick, yet once you take hold of it your entire body commits itself to the shaft.

sentences.zh: 故必以小腹貼桿，使主運；

translations.literal: Therefore the lower belly must press against the shaft and serve as the master of movement;
translations.idiomatic: The lower abdomen must press against the shaft and govern every motion;

sentences.zh: 後手必盡錞，以虎口實擫之；

translations.literal: the rear hand must extend fully, gripping firmly with the tiger's mouth;
translations.idiomatic: the rear hand must reach its full extension, the web of the thumb clamping the shaft;

sentences.zh: 前手必直，令盡勢。

translations.literal: the forward hand must be straight so that the force is fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: the leading hand must stay straight to release the full force.

sentences.zh: 以其掌根與後手虎口反正擰絞，而虛指使主導。

translations.literal: The root of the forward palm and the rear hand's tiger's mouth twist against each other in opposite directions, while the empty fingers serve as the guiding master.
translations.idiomatic: The base of the leading palm and the rear hand's grip twist against each other, while the open fingers guide the action.

sentences.zh: 兩足亦左虛右實，進退相任以趨勢。

translations.literal: Both feet likewise have the left empty and the right full, advancing and retreating in mutual support to seize momentum.
translations.idiomatic: The feet too keep the left empty and the right weighted, advance and retreat working together to carry the momentum.

sentences.zh: 使槍尖、前手尖、前足尖、鼻尖五尖相對，而五尺之身，自託廕於數寸之桿，遮閉周匝，敵仗無從入犯矣。

translations.literal: Align the spear tip, the forward hand's tip, the forward foot's tip, and the tip of the nose—the five tips facing one another—so that a five-foot body shelters itself upon a shaft of a few inches, closing off all around, and the enemy's weapon has no way to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Line up the spear point, the leading hand, the front foot, and the nose—the five points aligned—so that your five-foot frame shelters itself behind a shaft only inches thick, sealing every angle, and no enemy weapon can find a way in.

sentences.zh: 其用，有戳、有打；

translations.literal: In its use there are thrusting and striking;
translations.idiomatic: In application it may thrust or strike;

sentences.zh: 其法，曰二、曰叉。

translations.literal: Its method has two [techniques], called er and cha.
translations.idiomatic: The method comprises two techniques, called the strike and the cross.

sentences.zh: 二以取人，叉以拒人。

translations.literal: Er is used to seize the opponent; cha is used to repel the opponent.
translations.idiomatic: The strike seizes the opponent; the cross blocks him off.

sentences.zh: 此叉則彼二，此二則彼叉。

translations.literal: When one side uses cha, the other uses er; when one uses er, the other uses cha.
translations.idiomatic: When you cross, he strikes; when you strike, he crosses.

sentences.zh: 叉二循環，兩槍尖交如繞指，分寸間，出入百合，不得令相附。

translations.literal: Cha and er cycle in turn; the two spear tips meet like fingers interlaced, within inches advancing and retreating through a hundred exchanges, and must never be allowed to cling together.
translations.idiomatic: Strike and cross alternate in endless cycle; the spear points weave together like linked fingers, thrusting and withdrawing within inches through a hundred passes, and must never be allowed to lock.

sentences.zh: 桿一附，則有僕者，故曰'千金難買一聲響'。

translations.literal: Once the shafts cling together there is a fallen man, hence the saying, 'A thousand in gold cannot buy a single ringing clash.'
translations.idiomatic: Let the shafts stick once and someone falls—hence the proverb, 'No sum in gold can buy the sound of a clean strike.'

sentences.zh: 手同則爭目，目同則爭氣。

translations.literal: When the hands match, they contend with the eyes; when the eyes match, they contend with the breath.
translations.idiomatic: When hands are evenly matched, the contest shifts to the eyes; when eyes are evenly matched, it shifts to breath and spirit.

sentences.zh: 氣之運也，久暫稍殊，而勝敗分焉。

translations.literal: In the circulation of qi, endurance and brevity differ slightly, and victory and defeat are thereby divided.
translations.idiomatic: Breath and stamina differ only slightly over time, yet that small margin decides who wins and who loses.

sentences.zh: 故其術為至靜。

translations.literal: Therefore its art is utmost stillness.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the art demands the utmost calm.

sentences.zh: 」「吾授徒百數，而莫能傳吾術。

translations.literal: ""I have taught more than a hundred disciples, yet none could transmit my art.
translations.idiomatic: "I have taught more than a hundred disciples, yet none could truly pass on my art.

sentences.zh: 吾之術，受於師者才十之三，其十之七，則授徒時被其非法相取之勢迫而得之於無意者也。

translations.literal: Of my art, only three-tenths came from my master; the other seven-tenths I gained without intending it, when teaching disciples and being forced by their improper attempts to seize advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Only three-tenths of my art came from my master; the other seven-tenths I learned unawares while teaching, when disciples tried illicit tricks and the pressure of their gambits forced the answers from me.

sentences.zh: 是故名師易求，佳徒難訪。

translations.literal: Hence a famous master is easy to find, but a worthy disciple is hard to seek.
translations.idiomatic: That is why a famous master is easy to find, but a worthy disciple is hard to come by.

sentences.zh: 佳徒意在得師，以天下之大，求之無不如意者。

translations.literal: A worthy disciple aims to obtain a master; in a world so vast, he can seek one and find none who will disappoint him.
translations.idiomatic: A worthy disciple wants only to find a master; in all the world he can search until he finds one who satisfies him.

sentences.zh: 至名師求徒，雖遇高資妙質，足以授道，而非其志之所存，不能耐勞苦以要之永久，則百貢而百見卻矣。

translations.literal: But when a famous master seeks a disciple, even if he meets one of lofty talent and fine quality fit to receive the Way, unless that talent lies where the master's heart is set and the disciple can endure hardship to secure a lasting bond, the master will be repelled a hundred times for every hundred gifts offered.
translations.idiomatic: When a famous master seeks a disciple, he may meet someone gifted enough to receive the full transmission, yet unless the disciple shares his purpose and can endure hardship for the long term, the master will turn away a hundred times for every hundred courtesies offered.

sentences.zh: 佩言與竹齋同時處揚州，後歸歙，不知所終。

translations.literal: Peiyan and Zhuzhai lived in Yangzhou at the same time; later Peiyan returned to She, and no one knows how he ended.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyan and Zhuzhai were in Yangzhou at the same time; Peiyan later returned to She County, and his later fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 江之桐，字蘭崖，安徽和州人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhitong, style name Lanya, was a native of Hezhou, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhitong, whose style name was Lanya, came from Hezhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，傭於江寧賣餅家，嗜讀書，其主人異之。

translations.literal: At little more than ten years of age he was hired out to a cake-seller's household in Jiangning; he loved reading, and his employer marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his early teens he worked for a cake shop in Jiangning; he loved books, and his employer took notice.

sentences.zh: 招至家，居之樓上數年，讀左傳、國語、戰國策、史記、漢書、三國志畢。

translations.literal: The man brought him home and lodged him upstairs for several years, until he had finished the Zuo Commentary, Discourses of the States, Stratagems of the Warring States, Records of the Historian, History of the Han, and Records of the Three Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: The man took him in and kept him on the upper floor for years until he had read through the Zuo Commentary, Discourses of the States, Stratagems of the Warring States, Records of the Historian, History of the Han, and Records of the Three Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 乃謝主人去，自設小肆於市。

translations.literal: He then thanked his host and left, setting up a small shop in the market on his own.
translations.idiomatic: He then thanked his host and left to open a small shop in the market.

sentences.zh: 更習武藝，手​​臂刀矛，皆務實用，變通成法。

translations.literal: He further studied martial arts; with hand, arm, blade, and spear he sought only practical use and adapted established methods.
translations.idiomatic: He also trained in martial arts, working hand, arm, blade, and spear for practical effect and adapting the standard forms.

sentences.zh: 且讀書，且習藝，讀稍倦，則趫舉翕張，以作其氣。

translations.literal: He would read and practice the arts together; when reading wearied him slightly, he would leap and stretch, opening and closing the body to rouse his qi.
translations.idiomatic: He read and trained at once; when study tired him he would leap and stretch, flexing his limbs to stir his energy.

sentences.zh: 已而默坐，以凝其神，晝夜無間。

translations.literal: Then he would sit in silence to concentrate his spirit, without interruption day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Then he would sit in silence to focus his mind, day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 至百日乃睡，睡十餘日，復如之。

translations.literal: He would go a hundred days before sleeping, then sleep for more than ten days, and repeat the cycle.
translations.idiomatic: He would stay awake for a hundred days, then sleep for ten or more, and begin again.

sentences.zh: 讀史善疑，質之儒生，往往無以答。

translations.literal: In reading history he was skilled at raising doubts; when he questioned Confucian scholars, they often had no answer.
translations.idiomatic: He read history with a skeptical eye and would press scholars with his doubts, often leaving them without a reply.

sentences.zh: 其藝通綿長、俞刀、程棓、瓘嵋十八棍，多取洪門，敵硬鬥強，以急疾為用。

translations.literal: His arts embraced Mianchang, Yudao, Chengbang, and the eighteen staffs of Guanmei; he drew largely on Hongmen methods, meeting hardness with strength and relying on speed.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Mianchang, Yudao, Chengbang, and Guanmei eighteen-staff styles, drawing chiefly on Hongmen traditions—meeting force with force and prizing speed above all.

sentences.zh: 复及陣圖、形勢、器械，皆有理解。

translations.literal: He also had understanding of battle arrays, terrain and disposition, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He also understood battle formations, terrain, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 年六十餘，始遇荊溪周濟。

translations.literal: Past sixty years of age he first met Zhou Ji of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Not until he was past sixty did he meet Zhou Ji of Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 濟故績學，自負經世之略，通武藝，好談兵。

translations.literal: Ji was a scholar of long standing who prided himself on statecraft, was versed in martial arts, and loved to discuss warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji was a seasoned scholar who prided himself on practical statecraft, knew martial arts, and loved to talk of war.

sentences.zh: 與語大悅，延教其孫，三年而之桐卒。

translations.literal: Speaking with him, Ji was greatly pleased and invited him to teach his grandson; three years later Zhitong died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji delighted in their talks and asked him to instruct his grandson; three years later Zhitong died.

sentences.zh: 濟之言曰：「兵事至危，非得練士能臨敵苦鬥曆三十刻，及選鋒一可當三者，雖上有致果之志，下有死長之心，遇強敵不能必克。

translations.literal: Ji said, "Warfare is supremely perilous. Unless one has drilled soldiers who can face the enemy in bitter combat for thirty quarter-hours, and vanguard elites each equal to three men, then even if the commander above is resolved on victory and the troops below are ready to die for their leader, one cannot be sure of defeating a strong foe when meeting him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji said, "War is supremely dangerous. Unless you have drilled soldiers who can face the enemy in hard fighting for seven and a half hours straight, and elite vanguard troops each worth three ordinary men, then even if the commander above is bent on victory and the men below are ready to die for their leader, you cannot be sure of beating a strong enemy.

sentences.zh: 以力為本，以技濟之，謂之練士；

translations.literal: Taking strength as the foundation and skill to assist it—such men are called drilled soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Strength as the foundation, skill to support it—that is what makes drilled soldiers;

sentences.zh: 作其勇者，謂之選鋒。

translations.literal: rousing the brave among them—such men are called chosen vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: and rousing the brave among them—that is the chosen vanguard.

sentences.zh: 世之便騎射、習火器，以為士卒程，事取捷速，恆不能持久。

translations.literal: The world favors mounted archery and training in firearms as the standard for soldiers; affairs are pursued for quick results and usually cannot last.
translations.idiomatic: The world takes mounted archery and firearms training as the soldier's standard, chasing quick results that rarely endure.

sentences.zh: 洎乎接刃，則霍然而去。

translations.literal: When it comes to crossing blades, they flee in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: But when blades actually meet, they scatter at once.

sentences.zh: 故曰'巧不勝拙'。

translations.literal: Hence the saying, 'Cleverness cannot overcome clumsiness.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying, 'Cleverness cannot beat steady grit.'

sentences.zh: 若之桐，庶為知務。

translations.literal: As for Zhitong, he perhaps understood what truly matters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitong, it seems, understood what truly mattered.

sentences.zh: 梁九，順天人。

translations.literal: Liang Jiu was a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Jiu came from Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 自明末至清初，大內興造匠作，皆九董其役。

translations.literal: From the late Ming through the early Qing, all palace construction and craftsmen's work within the Inner Court was directed by Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Ming through the early Qing, all palace construction within the Inner Court fell under Jiu's direction.

sentences.zh: 初，明時京師有工師馮巧者，董造宮殿，至崇禎間老矣。

translations.literal: At first, in Ming times the capital had a master craftsman named Feng Qiao who oversaw palace building; by the Chongzhen reign he had grown old.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Ming times the capital had a master builder named Feng Qiao who oversaw the palaces; by the Chongzhen reign he had grown old.

sentences.zh: 九往執業門下，數載，終不得其傳，而服事左右，不懈益恭。

translations.literal: Jiu went to study under him for several years and never received the full transmission, yet he attended at his side without slackening and grew ever more respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu apprenticed under him for years without ever receiving the full transmission, yet he served at his side tirelessly and with growing deference.

sentences.zh: 一日九獨侍，巧顧曰：「子可教矣！

translations.literal: One day Jiu alone attended him; Qiao looked back and said, "You may now be taught!
translations.idiomatic: One day Jiu was attending him alone; Qiao turned and said, "You are ready to learn!

sentences.zh: 」於是盡授其奧。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he fully transmitted its inner mysteries.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he taught him everything he knew.

sentences.zh: 巧死，九遂隸籍工部，代執營造之事。

translations.literal: When Qiao died, Jiu was enrolled in the Ministry of Works and took over construction affairs in his place.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiao died, Jiu was entered on the rolls of the Ministry of Works and assumed responsibility for construction.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十四年，重建太和殿，九手製木殿一區，以寸準尺，以尺準丈，大不逾數尺許，四阿重室，規模悉其，工作以之為準，無爽。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Kangxi, when the Hall of Supreme Harmony was rebuilt, Jiu made a wooden model of the hall by hand, using the inch to calibrate the foot and the foot to calibrate the zhang; the whole was no more than a few chi across, with four-cornered roof and multiple chambers, complete in every feature of the design. The workmen took it as their standard, without the slightest deviation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Kangxi, when the Hall of Supreme Harmony was rebuilt, Jiu carved a wooden model by hand—inch scaling to foot, foot to zhang—no more than a few feet across, with its four-cornered roof and nested chambers reproducing the full design. The workmen used it as their standard, and not a measure was off.

sentences.zh: 張漣，字南垣，浙江秀水人，本籍江南華亭。

translations.literal: Zhang Lian, style name Nanyuan, was a native of Xiushui, Zhejiang, with his original household register in Huating, Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lian, whose style name was Nanyuan, was registered in Xiushui, Zhejiang, though his family originally came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少學畫，謁董其昌，通其法，用以疊石堆土為假山。

translations.literal: In youth he studied painting, called on Dong Qichang, mastered his methods, and applied them to piling stone and earth into artificial mountains.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied painting and sought out Dong Qichang; mastering his principles, he applied them to building rockeries from stacked stone and earth.

sentences.zh: 謂世之聚危石作洞壑者，氣象蹙促，由於不通畫理。

translations.literal: He said that those in the world who heap perilous stones into caves and ravines produce a cramped atmosphere because they do not understand painting principles.
translations.idiomatic: He said that rockeries built by heaping precarious stones into caves and gullies look cramped because their makers do not understand painting.

sentences.zh: 故漣所作，平岡小阪，陵阜陂纮​​，錯之以石，就其奔注起伏之勢，多得畫意，而石取易致，隨地材足，點綴飛動，變化無窮。

translations.literal: Therefore what Lian made were level knolls and low slopes, mounds and gentle banks, set with stones according to the rushing rise and fall of their flow, often achieving painterly effect; stones were chosen for easy procurement, materials sufficed wherever the site lay, and the ornament leapt with life in endless variation.
translations.idiomatic: Lian's gardens instead offered gentle knolls and low hills, mounds and rolling banks, with stones placed to follow the natural sweep of water and terrain—often achieving a painter's effect. He used stones easy to obtain and materials at hand on each site, and his accents danced with life in endless variation.

sentences.zh: 為之既久，土石草樹，咸識其性情，各得其用。

translations.literal: Having practiced this long, he knew the nature of earth, stone, grass, and trees, and each was put to its proper use.
translations.idiomatic: After long practice he knew the character of earth, stone, grass, and trees, and put each to its best use.

sentences.zh: 創手之始，亂石林立，躊躕四顧，默識在心。

translations.literal: At the start of a project, stones stood in disorder; he would pace about looking all around, the plan fixed silently in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of a job, with stones strewn everywhere, he would pace and look about, the whole design already clear in his mind.

sentences.zh: 高坐與客談笑，但呼役夫，某樹下某石置某處，不假斧鑿而合。

translations.literal: Seated high, he would talk and laugh with guests and merely call to the laborers to place such-and-such a stone under such-and-such a tree in such-and-such a spot; without relying on axe or chisel it would all fit together.
translations.idiomatic: He would sit chatting with guests and simply call to the workmen to set this stone under that tree in that spot—and without cutting or carving, everything fell into place.

sentences.zh: 及成，結構天然，奇正罔不入妙。

translations.literal: When finished, the structure was naturally formed, and every balance of the unexpected and the orthodox entered into mastery.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the composition looked utterly natural, every contrast of odd and regular falling into perfect harmony.

sentences.zh: 以其術游江以南數十年，大家名園，多出其手。

translations.literal: He practiced his art south of the Yangzi for several decades, and many great houses and famous gardens came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced his art south of the Yangzi for decades, and many of the great estates and famous gardens were his work.

sentences.zh: 東至越，北至燕，多慕其名來請者，四子皆衣食其業。

translations.literal: East to Yue and north to Yan, many who admired his name came to invite him; all four of his sons lived on his craft.
translations.idiomatic: From Yue in the east to Yan in the north, admirers sought him out by name, and all four of his sons lived by his trade.

sentences.zh: 晚歲，大學士馮銓聘赴京師，以老辭，遣其仲子往。

translations.literal: In his later years Grand Secretary Feng Quan invited him to the capital; he declined on account of age and sent his second son in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Grand Secretary Feng Quan invited him to Beijing; citing his age, he sent his second son instead.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，卒。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 後京師亦傳其法，有稱山石張者，世業百餘年未替。

translations.literal: Later his method spread in the capital as well; those called Zhang the Mountain-Stone Man kept the family trade for more than a hundred years without decline.
translations.idiomatic: Later his method spread in the capital too; the line known as Zhang the Rock-Master carried on the family trade for more than a century without interruption.

sentences.zh: 吳偉業、黃宗羲並為漣作傳，宗羲謂其「移山水畫法為石工，比元劉元之塑人物像，同為絕技」雲。

translations.literal: Wu Weiye and Huang Zongxi both wrote biographies of Lian; Zongxi said that he "transferred landscape-painting methods to stonework, comparable to Yuan Liu Yuan's sculpting of human figures—both supreme skills alike."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Weiye and Huang Zongxi both wrote his biography; Zongxi said he "transferred landscape painting to stonework, comparable to the Yuan master Liu Yuan's sculpture of human figures—each a supreme art in its kind."

sentences.zh: 葉陶，字金城，江南青浦人，本籍新安。

translations.literal: Ye Tao, style name Jincheng, was a native of Qingpu in Jiangnan, with his original household register in Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Tao, whose style name was Jincheng, was registered in Qingpu in Jiangnan, though his family originally came from Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 善畫山水，康熙中，祇候內廷。

translations.literal: He was skilled at landscape painting; during Kangxi he attended at the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at landscape painting and during the Kangxi reign served at the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 奉敕作暢春園圖本稱旨，即命佐監造，園成，賜金馳驛歸。

translations.literal: By imperial order he painted a design for the Changchun Garden that pleased the throne; he was immediately appointed to assist in supervising construction, and when the garden was finished he was given gold and sent home by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he painted a design for the Changchun Garden that pleased the emperor; he was then appointed to help supervise its construction, and when the garden was finished he received gold and was sent home by courier.

sentences.zh: 尋復召，卒於途。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned again and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned again but died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 劉源，字伴阮，河南祥符人，隸漢軍旗籍。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan, style name Banruan, was a native of Xiangfu, Henan, enrolled in a Han Banner register.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan, whose style name was Banruan, came from Xiangfu in Henan and was registered in a Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，官刑部主事，供奉內廷，監督蕪湖、九江兩關，技巧絕倫。

translations.literal: During Kangxi he held the post of principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, attended at the Inner Court, supervised the Wuhu and Jiujiang customs stations, and his craftsmanship was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he served as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, attended at court, supervised the Wuhu and Jiujiang customs posts, and his skill was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 少工畫，曾繪唐凌煙閣功臣像，鐫刻行世，吳偉業贈詩紀之。

translations.literal: In youth he worked at painting; he once painted portraits of the Tang dynasty's Lingyange meritorious officials, had them engraved and circulated, and Wu Weiye presented a poem to commemorate them.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he painted; he once depicted the Tang meritorious officials of Lingyan Pavilion, had the images engraved and published, and Wu Weiye wrote a poem to commemorate the work.

sentences.zh: 及在內廷，於殿壁畫竹，風枝雨葉，極生動之致，為時所稱。

translations.literal: When he was at the Inner Court he painted bamboo on palace walls; wind-tossed branches and rain-beaten leaves reached the utmost vividness and won praise in his day.
translations.idiomatic: At court he painted bamboo on palace walls—wind-lashed branches and rain-swept leaves so vivid that contemporaries praised them highly.

sentences.zh: 手製清煙墨，在「寥天一」、「青麟髓」之上。

translations.literal: He made clear-smoke ink by hand, surpassing the brands "Vast Sky One" and "Blue Unicorn Marrow."
translations.idiomatic: He made his own clear-smoke ink by hand, finer than the celebrated brands Liaotianyi and Qinglinsui.

sentences.zh: 於一笏上刻滕王閣序、心經，字畫嶄然。

translations.literal: On a single tablet he engraved the Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng and the Heart Sutra; the characters and lines stood out sharp and clear.
translations.idiomatic: On a single tablet he engraved the Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng and the Heart Sutra, every character crisp and clear.

sentences.zh: 奉敕制太皇太后及皇貴妃寶範，撥蠟精絕。

translations.literal: By imperial order he made the imperial seals for the Grand Empress Dowager and the Imperial Noble Consort; his lost-wax casting was consummate.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he cast the seals for the Grand Empress Dowager and the Imperial Noble Consort, his lost-wax work unsurpassed.

sentences.zh: 時江西景德鎮開御窯，源呈赩樣數百種。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial kiln was opened at Jingdezhen in Jiangxi, and Yuan submitted several hundred glazed color patterns.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial kiln opened at Jingdezhen in Jiangxi, Yuan submitted several hundred glaze designs.

sentences.zh: 參古今之式，運以新意，備諸巧妙。

translations.literal: He drew on forms ancient and modern, applied fresh ideas, and equipped every refinement of ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: He drew on forms old and new, infused them with fresh invention, and mastered every refinement.

sentences.zh: 於彩繪人物山水花鳥，尤各極其勝。

translations.literal: In polychrome painting of figures, landscapes, flowers, and birds he especially brought each to its finest excellence.
translations.idiomatic: In polychrome figures, landscapes, flowers, and birds he brought each to its highest perfection.

sentences.zh: 及成，其精美過於明代諸窯。

translations.literal: When finished, their refinement surpassed the kilns of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the wares surpassed even the finest Ming kilns.

sentences.zh: 其他御用木漆器物，亦多出監作，聖祖甚眷遇之。

translations.literal: Other imperial objects in wood and lacquer likewise mostly came from his supervision, and the Sacred Ancestor favored him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Other imperial wood and lacquer pieces also largely came under his supervision, and the Kangxi Emperor favored him warmly.

sentences.zh: 及卒，無子，命官奠茶酒，侍衛護柩，馳驛歸葬，恩禮特異焉。

translations.literal: When he died he had no son; officials were ordered to offer tea and wine, bodyguards to escort the coffin, and an express relay to return him for burial—the favor shown was altogether exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons; officials were ordered to offer libations, guards to escort the coffin, and couriers to carry him home for burial—honors rarely granted.

sentences.zh: 唐英，字俊公，漢軍旗人。

translations.literal: Tang Ying, style name Jungong, was a man of the Han Banners.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ying, whose style name was Jungong, belonged to the Han Banners.

sentences.zh: 官內務府員外郎，直養心殿。

translations.literal: He held the post of vice director in the Imperial Household Department and served on duty at the Hall of Mental Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a vice director of the Imperial Household Department and attended at the Hall of Mental Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，命監江西景德鎮窯務，歷監粵海關、淮安關。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he was ordered to supervise the kiln affairs of Jingdezhen in Jiangxi, and successively supervised the Guangdong maritime customs and the Huai'an customs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he was appointed to supervise the Jingdezhen kilns in Jiangxi, and later oversaw the Guangdong maritime customs and the Huai'an customs as well.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，調九江關，复監督窯務，先後在事十餘年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he was transferred to the Jiujiang customs and again supervised kiln affairs; altogether he was in charge for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he was moved to the Jiujiang customs and again took charge of the kilns, serving in all for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 明以中官督造，後改巡道，督府佐司其事，清初因之。

translations.literal: In the Ming, eunuchs supervised manufacture; later this was changed to circuit intendants, with provincial deputies assisting in the matter—the early Qing followed the same practice.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, eunuchs supervised production; later circuit intendants took over, with provincial deputies assisting—the early Qing followed the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 順治中，巡撫郎廷佐所督造，精美有名，世稱「郎窯」。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi, what was supervised by Governor Lang Tingzuo was famed for refinement and was called in the world the "Lang Kiln."
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi, wares supervised by Governor Lang Tingzuo were famed for their beauty and came to be known as Lang ware.

sentences.zh: 其後御窯興工，每命工部或內務府司官往，專任其事。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever the imperial kiln undertook work, an official of the Ministry of Works or the Imperial Household Department was sent to take sole charge.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the imperial kiln went into production, an official from the Ministry of Works or the Imperial Household Department was dispatched to take sole charge.

sentences.zh: 年希堯曾奉使造器甚夥，世稱「年窯」。

translations.literal: Nian Xiyao once received a commission and produced a great many vessels, called in the world the "Nian Kiln."
translations.idiomatic: Nian Xiyao once received an imperial commission and produced a great quantity of ware, known as Nian ware.

sentences.zh: 英繼其後，任事最久，講求陶法，於泥土、釉料、坯胎、火候，具有心得，躬自指揮。

translations.literal: Ying followed after him, held office longest, studied ceramic methods thoroughly, and had true understanding of clay, glaze, biscuit body, and firing heat, directing everything in person.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ying followed him and served longest; he studied ceramic technique thoroughly and understood clay, glaze, body, and firing from experience, directing every stage himself.

sentences.zh: 又能卹工慎帑，撰陶成紀事碑，備載經費、工匠解額，臚列諸色赩釉，仿古採今，凡五十七種。

translations.literal: He could also show compassion to workers and be careful with treasury funds; he composed the Stele on Ceramic Achievements, fully recording expenditures and craftsmen's quotas, enumerating every colored glaze—drawing on antiquity and selecting from the present—in all fifty-seven kinds.
translations.idiomatic: He also cared for the workers and guarded the treasury carefully; he wrote the Stele on Ceramic Achievements, recording costs and craftsmen's quotas and listing every glaze color—drawing on antiquity and the present—in all fifty-seven varieties.

sentences.zh: 自宋大觀，明永樂、宣德、成化、嘉靖、萬曆諸官窯，及哥窯、定窯、均窯、龍泉窯、宜興窯、西洋、東洋諸器，皆有仿製。

translations.literal: From the Song Daguan reign through the Ming official kilns of Yongle, Xuande, Chenghua, Jiajing, and Wanli, as well as Ge, Ding, Jun, Longquan, and Yixing kilns and wares of the Western and Eastern Oceans—all were reproduced.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song Daguan ware through the Ming official kilns of Yongle, Xuande, Chenghua, Jiajing, and Wanli, as well as Ge, Ding, Jun, Longquan, and Yixing wares and pieces from Europe and Japan—he reproduced them all.

sentences.zh: 其釉色，有白粉青、大綠、米色、玫瑰紫、海棠紅、茄花紫、梅子青、騾肝、馬肺、天藍、霽紅、霽青、鱔魚黃、蛇皮綠​​、油綠、歐紅、歐藍、月白、翡翠、烏金、紫金諸種。

translations.literal: Among his glaze colors were white powder-blue, great green, rice color, rose purple, crab-apple red, eggplant-flower purple, plum green, mule-liver, horse-lung, sky blue, rain-cleared red, rain-cleared blue, eel yellow, snake-skin green, oil green, Ou red, Ou blue, moon white, jadeite, black gold, purple gold, and other kinds.
translations.idiomatic: His glaze colors included white powder-blue, deep green, rice, rose purple, crab-apple red, eggplant purple, plum green, mule-liver, horse-lung, sky blue, rain-cleared red and blue, eel yellow, snake-skin green, oil green, Ou red and blue, moon white, jadeite, black gold, purple gold, and many more.

sentences.zh: 又有澆黃、澆紫、澆綠、填白、描金、青花、水墨、五彩、錐花、拱花、抹金、抹銀諸名。

translations.literal: There were also the names poured yellow, poured purple, poured green, filled white, gilt tracing, blue-and-white, ink wash, five colors, incised flower, raised flower, applied gold, and applied silver.
translations.idiomatic: There were also poured yellow, purple, and green, filled white, gilt tracing, blue-and-white, ink wash, five-color, incised and raised floral designs, and applied gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 奉敕編陶冶圖，為圖二十：曰採石製泥，曰淘煉泥土，曰煉灰配釉，曰製造匣缽，曰圓器修模，曰圓器拉坯，曰琢器做坯，曰採取青料，曰煉選青料，曰印坯乳料，曰圓器青花，曰制畫琢器，曰蘸釉吹釉，曰鏇坯挖足，曰成坯入窯，曰燒坯開窯，曰圓琢洋採，曰明爐暗爐，曰束草裝桶，曰祀神酬原。

translations.literal: By imperial order he compiled Illustrations of Ceramic Craft, with twenty plates: quarrying stone to make clay; washing and refining clay; refining ash to mix glaze; making saggers; trimming roundware molds; throwing roundware; shaping carved ware; gathering cobalt ore; refining and selecting cobalt; stamping bodies and grinding slip; blue-and-white roundware; designing and painting carved ware; dipping and blowing glaze; turning the foot; placing finished bodies in the kiln; firing and opening the kiln; round and carved ware with foreign colors; open and closed kilns; bundling straw and packing barrels; and sacrificing to the gods to repay origins.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he compiled Illustrations of Ceramic Craft in twenty plates: quarrying and preparing clay; washing and refining clay; preparing glaze ash; making saggers; trimming roundware molds; throwing roundware; shaping carved ware; gathering cobalt; refining cobalt; stamping bodies and preparing slip; blue-and-white roundware; painting carved ware; dipping and blowing glaze; turning the foot; loading the kiln; firing and opening the kiln; foreign-color round and carved ware; open and closed kilns; packing for transport; and offerings to the kiln gods.

sentences.zh: 各附詳說，備著工作次第，後之治陶政者取法焉。

translations.literal: Each was provided with detailed explanation, fully setting forth the order of work, so that later overseers of ceramic affairs might take it as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Each plate had a detailed explanation setting out the sequence of work, so that later supervisors of the kilns could take it as their guide.

sentences.zh: 英所造者，世稱「唐窯」。

translations.literal: What Ying made was called in the world the "Tang Kiln."
translations.idiomatic: Wares from his tenure came to be known as Tang ware.

sentences.zh: 戴梓，字文開，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Dai Zi, style name Wenkai, was a native of Qiantang, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zi, whose style name was Wenkai, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少有機悟，自製火器，能擊百步外。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick-witted; he made firearms of his own that could strike beyond a hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was ingenious; he built his own firearms that could hit targets more than a hundred paces away.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，耿精忠叛，犯浙江，康親王杰書南征，梓以布衣從軍，獻連珠火銃法。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, Geng Jingzhong rebelled and invaded Zhejiang; Prince Kang Jieshu marched south, and Zi followed the army as a commoner, presenting his method for the serial-fire musket.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign, when Geng Jingzhong rebelled and invaded Zhejiang, Prince Kang Jieshu marched south; Dai Zi joined the campaign as a civilian and presented his design for a repeating musket.

sentences.zh: 下江山有功，授道員劄付。

translations.literal: He had merit in capturing Jiangshan and was given a commissioner's patent of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the capture of Jiangshan and received a commissioner's patent of appointment.

sentences.zh: 師還，聖祖召見，知其能文，試春日早朝詩，稱旨，授翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Sacred Ancestor summoned him, learned that he could write, tested him with a poem on the spring morning court audience, found it pleasing, and appointed him Hanlin Academy expositor.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the emperor summoned him, learned that he could write, tested him with a poem on the spring morning audience, was pleased, and appointed him a Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 偕高士奇入直南書房，尋改直養心殿。

translations.literal: Together with Gao Shiqi he entered duty at the Southern Studios; soon he was transferred to duty at the Hall of Mental Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Gao Shiqi in the Southern Studios and was soon transferred to the Hall of Mental Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 梓通天文算法，預纂修律呂正義，與南懷仁及諸西洋人論不合，咸忌之。

translations.literal: Zi was versed in astronomy and calculation, took part in compiling the Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes, and disagreed in debate with Ferdinand Verbiest and the other Westerners—all bore him resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zi knew astronomy and mathematics, helped compile the Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes, and clashed in debate with Ferdinand Verbiest and the other Jesuits, who all came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 陳弘勳者，張獻忠養子，投誠得官，向梓索詐，互毆構訟。

translations.literal: There was one Chen Hongxun, an adopted son of Zhang Xianzhong who had surrendered and received office; he demanded extortion from Zi, they beat each other, and brought lawsuits against one another.
translations.idiomatic: One Chen Hongxun, an adopted son of Zhang Xianzhong who had surrendered and received an official post, tried to extort money from Dai Zi; they came to blows and brought lawsuits against each other.

sentences.zh: 忌者中以蜚語，褫職，徙關東。

translations.literal: Those who resented him lodged slanderous talk; he was stripped of office and exiled to the eastern passes.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies spread rumors against him; he was dismissed from office and banished to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 後赦還家，留於鐵嶺，遂隸籍。

translations.literal: Later, after an amnesty, he returned home, remained at Tieling, and was entered on the local register.
translations.idiomatic: He was later pardoned and went home, but stayed on at Tieling and was enrolled in the local household rolls.

sentences.zh: 所造連珠銃，形如琵琶，火藥鉛丸，皆貯於銃脊，以機輪開閉。

translations.literal: The serial-fire musket he made was shaped like a pipa; gunpowder and lead balls were all stored along the gun's spine and admitted or shut off by geared wheels.
translations.idiomatic: His repeating musket was shaped like a pipa, with powder and shot stored along the barrel and fed by a geared mechanism.

sentences.zh: 其機有二，相銜如牝牡，扳一機則火藥鉛丸自落筒中，第二機隨之並動，石激火出而銃發，凡二十八發乃重貯。

translations.literal: It had two mechanisms, interlocking like male and female; pulling one let powder and ball drop into the barrel, the second moved with it, flint struck fire, and the piece discharged—after twenty-eight shots one reloaded.
translations.idiomatic: Two interlocking triggers worked in tandem: the first dropped powder and ball into the chamber, the second followed, the flint sparked, and the gun fired; after twenty-eight rounds it had to be reloaded.

sentences.zh: 法與西洋機關槍合，當時未通用，器藏於家，乾隆中猶存。

translations.literal: The principle matched the Western machine-gun, but it was not adopted in his day; the weapon was kept at home and still survived in the Qianlong era.
translations.idiomatic: The design matched that of a Western machine gun, though it never came into general use; the piece was kept in his household and was still in existence under Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 西洋人貢蟠腸鳥槍，梓奉命仿造，以十槍賚其使臣。

translations.literal: Westerners presented coiled-barrel muskets as tribute; Zi was ordered to copy them and rewarded the envoys with ten guns.
translations.idiomatic: When Westerners presented coiled-barrel muskets as tribute, Dai Zi was ordered to reproduce them and sent ten muskets back to their envoys.

sentences.zh: 又奉命造子母砲，母送子出墜而碎裂，如西洋炸砲，聖祖率諸臣親臨視之，錫名為「威遠將軍」，鐫制者職名於砲後。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to make mother-and-child cannon: the mother expelled the child, which fell and burst apart like a Western shell-gun; the Sacred Ancestor led his ministers to view it in person, bestowed the name "General Might-from-Afars," and had the maker's office title cut on the rear of the gun.
translations.idiomatic: He was also commissioned to build a mother-and-child cannon whose shell burst on impact like a Western explosive shell; the Kangxi Emperor came in person with his ministers to inspect it, named it the "General Might-from-Afars," and had Dai Zi's official title engraved on the breech.

sentences.zh: 親征噶爾丹，用以破敵。

translations.literal: On the campaign in person against Galdan, it was used to break the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: It was employed to defeat the foe when the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 丁守存，字心齋，山東日照人。

translations.literal: Ding Shoucun, style name Xinzhai, was a native of Rizhao, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shoucun, whose style name was Xinzhai, came from Rizhao in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，授戶部主事，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and served as a secretarial clerk on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1835, was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and served on the staff of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 守存通天文、曆算、風角、壬遁之術，善製器。

translations.literal: Shoucun was versed in astronomy, calendrical calculation, wind-angle divination, and ren-dun arts, and was skilled at making instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucun mastered astronomy, calendrical science, wind divination, and esoteric prognostication, and excelled at mechanical invention.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利兵犯沿海數省，船砲之利，為中國所未有。

translations.literal: At that time English troops were attacking several coastal provinces; the advantage of their ships and cannon was something China had never had.
translations.idiomatic: When British forces struck several coastal provinces, the superiority of their warships and artillery was unlike anything China had yet faced.

sentences.zh: 守存慨然講求製造，西學猶未通行，凡所謂力學、化學、光學、重學，皆無專書，覃思每與闇合。

translations.literal: Shoucun set himself earnestly to study manufacture; Western learning was not yet widespread, and for what are called mechanics, chemistry, optics, and ponderous science there were no specialized books—yet his deep reflection often coincided with them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucun threw himself into arms manufacture; Western science was still little known in China, and there were no textbooks on mechanics, chemistry, optics, or gravitation—yet his own painstaking thought often arrived at the same conclusions.

sentences.zh: 大學士卓秉恬薦之，命繕進圖說，偕郎中文康、徐有壬赴天津，監造地雷、火機等器，試之皆驗。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhuo Bingtian recommended him; he was ordered to draft and submit illustrated explanations, and together with Director Wen Kang and Xu Youren went to Tianjin to supervise the making of land mines, fire engines, and other devices—all proved effective in trial.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhuo Bingtian recommended him; he was told to prepare illustrated specifications and, with Directors Wen Kang and Xu Youren, went to Tianjin to oversee production of land mines, firearms, and other weapons, all of which passed their trials.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從大學士賽尚阿赴廣西參軍事，會獲賊黨胡以暘，使招降其兄以晄，守存制一

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he followed Grand Secretary Saishang'a to Guangxi to take part in military affairs; when the rebel associate Hu Yiyang was captured, they had him induce his elder brother Yihuang to surrender; Shoucun made one
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he followed Grand Secretary Saishang'a to Guangxi on campaign; when the rebel Hu Yiyang was taken, they used him to lure his elder brother Yihuang to defect; Shoucun devised a

sentences.zh: 匣曰手捧雷，偽若緘書其中，俾以晄致之賊酋，酋啟匣炸首死。

translations.literal: case called the Hand-held Thunder, made to look as if a sealed letter were inside, had Yihuang deliver it to the rebel chief; the chief opened the case, the blast shattered his head, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: box called the Hand-held Thunder, disguised as if it held a sealed letter, and had Yihuang present it to the rebel leader; when the leader opened it, the explosion blew off his head and killed him.

sentences.zh: 尋檻送賊渠洪大全還京，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he escorted the rebel chieftain Hong Daquan back to the capital in a cage-cart and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He soon conveyed the rebel leader Hong Daquan to the capital in a prisoner cart and was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 從尚書孫瑞珍赴山東治沂州團防，造石雷、石砲以御賊。

translations.literal: He followed Minister Sun Ruizhen to Shandong to manage militia defense at Yizhou, and made stone thunder-bombs and stone cannon to repel bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Minister Sun Ruizhen to Shandong to organize militia defense at Yizhou, building stone mines and stone cannon to hold off the rebels.

sentences.zh: 尋調直隸襄辦團練，上戰守十六策。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Zhili to assist in organizing militia training and submitted sixteen strategies for attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to Zhili to help organize local militias and presented sixteen proposals on offensive and defensive warfare.

sentences.zh: 十年，回山東，創議築堡日照要塞，曰濤雒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he returned to Shandong, proposed building a fortified stronghold as a Rizhao bastion, and called it Taoluo.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he went back to Shandong and proposed a fortified bastion for Rizhao, named Taoluo.

sentences.zh: 賊大舉來犯，發石砲，聲震山谷，賊辟易，相戒無犯。

translations.literal: When bandits came in force to attack, the stone cannon were fired; the sound shook the valleys, the bandits gave way in fear, and warned one another not to trespass.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked in force, the stone cannon were fired; the roar echoed through the valleys, the enemy fell back in alarm, and they warned one another to keep away.

sentences.zh: 丁家堡附近之民歸之，數年遂成​​都聚。

translations.literal: The people near Dingjiabao came to him for refuge, and within a few years it became a large settlement.
translations.idiomatic: People from the vicinity of Dingjiabao flocked to him, and within a few years the place grew into a substantial town.

sentences.zh: 同治初，復至直隸，留治廣平防務，築堡二百餘所。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he returned to Zhili, remained to manage the defenses of Guangping, and built more than two hundred forts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign he went back to Zhili, stayed to oversee Guangping's defenses, and erected more than two hundred fortified posts.

sentences.zh: 軍事竣，授湖北督糧道，署按察使。

translations.literal: When military affairs were concluded, he was appointed grain-intendant of Hubei and acted as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaigns ended he was made Hubei's grain-intendant and served as acting provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 充鄉試監試，創法，以竹筒引江水注闈中，時以為便。

translations.literal: Serving as supervisor of the provincial examination, he devised a method of drawing river water into the examination compound through bamboo pipes, which people at the time found convenient.
translations.idiomatic: As chief examiner of the provincial civil service test, he devised a system of bamboo pipes to bring river water into the examination grounds, which contemporaries hailed as a great convenience.

sentences.zh: 瀕江諸省，率仿行之。

translations.literal: The provinces along the rivers generally followed his example.
translations.idiomatic: Riverine provinces across the country soon adopted the practice.

sentences.zh: 尋罷歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed and went home.

sentences.zh: 所著書曰丙丁秘籥，進禦不傳於外；

translations.literal: Among his writings was the Bingding Secret Register, presented to the throne and not circulated outside;
translations.idiomatic: His writings included the Bingding Secret Register, presented to the throne and kept from public circulation;

sentences.zh: 所傳者曰造化究原，曰新火器說。

translations.literal: those circulated were called Origins of Creation and Transformation and A Treatise on New Fire-Arms.
translations.idiomatic: those that did circulate were Origins of Creation and Transformation and A Treatise on New Fire-Arms.

sentences.zh: 徐壽，字雪村，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Xu Shou, style name Xuecun, was a native of Wuxi, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shou, whose style name was Xuecun, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 生於僻鄉，幼孤，事母以孝聞。
