translations.literal: Born in a remote village, orphaned young, he was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in an out-of-the-way hamlet, lost his father in childhood, and was famed for devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 性質直無華。

translations.literal: His nature was plain and unadorned.
translations.idiomatic: He was plainspoken and unpretentious by nature.

sentences.zh: 道、咸間，東南兵事起，遂棄舉業，專研博物格致之學。

translations.literal: Between the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns, when warfare broke out in the southeast, he abandoned the examination path and devoted himself solely to natural history and the investigation of things.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting engulfed the southeast in the Daoguang and Xianfeng eras, he gave up the civil service examinations and devoted himself entirely to natural science.

sentences.zh: 時泰西學術流傳中國者，尚未昌明，試驗諸器絕鮮。

translations.literal: At the time Western learning circulating in China was not yet flourishing, and apparatus for experiment was exceedingly rare.
translations.idiomatic: Western science had not yet taken firm root in China, and experimental equipment was almost impossible to find.

sentences.zh: 壽與金匱華蘅芳討論搜求，始得十一，苦心研索，每以意求之，而得其真。

translations.literal: Shou, together with Hua Hengfang of Jintan, discussed and sought them out, at first obtaining eleven; he studied them with bitter effort, often inferring by thought, and grasped their truth.
translations.idiomatic: Shou and Hua Hengfang of Jintan hunted them down together and at first found only eleven; through painstaking study he often reasoned his way to the truth.

sentences.zh: 嘗購三棱玻璃不可得，磨水晶印章成三角形，驗得光分七色。

translations.literal: Once he could not obtain a triangular prism of glass; he ground a crystal seal-stone into a triangle and verified that light splits into seven colors.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to buy a glass prism, he ground a crystal seal into a triangle and proved that light separates into seven colors.

sentences.zh: 知槍彈之行拋物線，疑其仰攻俯擊有異，設遠近多靶以測之，其成學之艱類此。

translations.literal: Knowing that bullets travel in parabolic paths, he doubted whether firing upward or downward made a difference, set up many targets at varying distances to test it—the hardships of mastering learning were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that bullets follow a parabolic trajectory, he wondered whether shooting uphill or downhill made a difference and set up targets at many ranges to find out; most of his scientific breakthroughs came at such cost.

sentences.zh: 久之，於西學具窺見原委，尤精製器。

translations.literal: After a long time he had gained a full view of the principles of Western learning and was especially skilled at making instruments.
translations.idiomatic: In time he came to grasp the fundamentals of Western science and proved especially gifted at mechanical invention.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，從大學士曾國籓軍，先後於安慶、江寧設機器局，皆預其事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng he followed Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan's army; machine bureaus were set up successively at Anqing and Jiangning, and he took part in all of them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he joined Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan's forces and helped establish arsenals at Anqing and later Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 壽與蘅芳及吳嘉廉、龔芸棠試造木質輪船，推求動理，測算汽機，蘅芳之力為多；

translations.literal: Shou, together with Hengfang, Wu Jialian, and Gong Yuntang, tried to build a wooden paddle steamer, worked out the laws of motion, and calculated the steam engine—Hengfang contributed the greater share of the effort;
translations.idiomatic: Shou, Hengfang, Wu Jialian, and Gong Yuntang experimented with a wooden steamer, working out the laws of motion and calculating the steam engine, with Hengfang contributing most of the theory;

sentences.zh: 造器罝機，皆出壽手製，不假西人，數年而成。

translations.literal: making the apparatus and installing the machinery all came from Shou's own hand, without relying on Westerners, and was completed in several years.
translations.idiomatic: but Shou built the machinery and installed the engines with his own hands, without Western help, and the vessel was finished after several years.

sentences.zh: 長五十餘尺，每一時能行四十餘裡，名之曰黃鵠。

translations.literal: It was more than fifty feet long and could travel more than forty li in an hour; they named it the Yellow Swan.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty feet long, it could cover over forty li an hour and was named the Yellow Swan.

sentences.zh: 國籓激賞之，招入幕府，以奇才異能薦。

translations.literal: Guofan was deeply impressed, summoned him into his staff, and recommended him for rare talent and unusual ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was delighted, brought him onto his staff, and recommended him as a man of extraordinary gifts.

sentences.zh: 既而設製造局於上海，百事草創，壽於船砲槍彈，多所發明。

translations.literal: Later a manufacturing bureau was set up at Shanghai; with everything newly begun, Shou made many inventions in ships, cannon, muskets, and ammunition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangnan Arsenal was founded in Shanghai, Shou devised many innovations in ships, artillery, firearms, and ammunition.

sentences.zh: 自製強水棉花藥、汞爆藥。

translations.literal: He himself made aqua fortis, guncotton, and mercury fulminate.
translations.idiomatic: He produced nitric acid, guncotton, and mercury fulminate on his own.

sentences.zh: 創議繙譯西書，以求製造根本。

translations.literal: He proposed translating Western books in order to secure the foundations of manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: He urged translating Western books to lay the foundations of modern industry.

sentences.zh: 於是聘西士偉力亞利、傅蘭雅、林樂知、金楷理等，壽與同志華蘅芳、李鳳苞、王德均、趙元益孳孳研究，先後成書數百種。

translations.literal: Thereupon Western scholars such as Alexander Wylie, John Fryer, Young J. Allen, and Carl T. Kreyer were engaged; Shou, with his comrades Hua Hengfang, Li Fengbao, Wang Dejun, and Zhao Yuanyi, studied tirelessly, and in succession completed several hundred works.
translations.idiomatic: Western scholars including Alexander Wylie, John Fryer, Young J. Allen, and Carl T. Kreyer were hired; Shou worked tirelessly with Hua Hengfang, Li Fengbao, Wang Dejun, and Zhao Yuanyi, and together they produced several hundred books.

sentences.zh: 壽所譯述者，曰西藝知新及續編，化學鑑原及續編、補編，化學考質，化學求數，物體遇熱改易說，汽機發軔，營陣揭要，測地繪圖，寶藏興焉。

translations.literal: Among Shou's translations and expositions were New Knowledge of Western Arts and its continuations, Elements of Chemistry and its continuations and supplements, Examination of Chemical Substances, Chemical Calculation, On the Alteration of Bodies by Heat, Introduction to the Steam Engine, Essentials of Camp Array, Surveying and Mapping, and On the Wealth of Nations.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's translations included New Knowledge of Western Arts and its sequels, Elements of Chemistry and its supplements, Examination of Chemical Substances, Chemical Calculation, On the Alteration of Bodies by Heat, Introduction to the Steam Engine, Essentials of Camp Array, Surveying and Mapping, and On the Wealth of Nations.

sentences.zh: 法律、醫學，刊行者凡十三種，西藝知新、化學鑑原二書，尤稱善本。

translations.literal: On law and medicine, thirteen works were published in all; the two books New Knowledge of Western Arts and Elements of Chemistry were especially praised as fine editions.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen works on law and medicine were published; New Knowledge of Western Arts and Elements of Chemistry were especially acclaimed as model translations.

sentences.zh: 同治末，與傅蘭雅設格致書院於上海，風氣漸開，成就甚眾，壽名益播。

translations.literal: Late in Tongzhi, together with John Fryer he founded the Polytechnic Academy in Shanghai; the climate of learning gradually opened, many were trained, and Shou's fame spread further.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tongzhi reign he and John Fryer founded the Polytechnic Academy in Shanghai; as scientific education took hold and many students flourished, Shou's reputation grew still wider.

sentences.zh: 山東、四川仿設​​機器局，爭延聘壽主其事，以譯書事尤急，皆謝不往，而使其子建寅、華封代行。

translations.literal: Shandong and Sichuan followed suit in setting up machine bureaus and vied to engage Shou to head them; because translation work was especially urgent, he declined all such offers and sent his sons Jianyin and Huafeng in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong and Sichuan set up their own arsenals and competed to hire Shou to run them; translation work kept him too busy to accept, and he sent his sons Jianyin and Huafeng instead.

sentences.zh: 大冶煤鐵礦、開平煤礦、漠河金礦經始之際，壽皆為擘畫規制。

translations.literal: At the founding of the Daye coal-iron mine, the Kaiping coal mine, and the Mohe gold mine, Shou drew up the plans and regulations for all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daye iron and coal works, the Kaiping coal mines, and the Mohe gold fields were first launched, Shou drafted the plans and specifications for each.

sentences.zh: 購器選匠，資其力焉。

translations.literal: He procured equipment and selected craftsmen, lending his strength to the effort.
translations.idiomatic: He helped purchase machinery and recruit skilled workers for all three ventures.

sentences.zh: 無錫產桑宜蠶，西商購繭奪民利，壽考求烘繭法，倡設烘灶，及機器繅絲法，育蠶者利驟增。

translations.literal: Wuxi produced mulberry suited to silkworms, but Western merchants bought cocoons and seized the people's profit; Shou investigated methods of drying cocoons, advocated setting up drying kilns, and machine reeling, and sericulturists' profits rose sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi's mulberry groves were ideal for sericulture, but Western merchants buying raw cocoons were squeezing local growers; Shou developed cocoon-drying methods, promoted drying ovens and mechanical reeling, and silkworm farmers' profits rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 壽狷介，不求仕進，以布衣終。

translations.literal: Shou was aloof and upright, sought no advancement in office, and ended his days as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was proud and independent, never sought official rank, and died a private citizen.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu era he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Guangxu reign, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子建寅、華封，皆世其學。

translations.literal: His sons Jianyin and Huafeng both inherited his learning.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jianyin and Huafeng both carried on his work.

sentences.zh: 建寅，字仲虎。

translations.literal: Jianyin, style name Zhonghu.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyin, whose style name was Zhonghu.

sentences.zh: 從父於江寧、上海，助任製造。

translations.literal: He followed his father to Jiangning and Shanghai and assisted in manufacturing duties.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father to Nanjing and Shanghai and helped run the arsenals.

sentences.zh: 尋充山東機器局總辦，福建船政提調，出使德國二等參贊，洊擢直隸候補道。

translations.literal: He soon served as general manager of the Shandong machine bureau, superintendent of the Fujian naval dockyard, second-class counselor on the mission to Germany, and was repeatedly promoted to expectant circuit intendant of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He later headed the Shandong arsenal, supervised the Fujian Naval Dockyard, served as second secretary on the mission to Germany, and rose repeatedly to expectant circuit intendant of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 光緒末，張之洞調至湖北監造無菸火藥，已成，藥炸裂，殞焉，賜優恤。

translations.literal: Late in Guangxu, Zhang Zhidong transferred him to Hubei to supervise the manufacture of smokeless powder; when it was finished the powder exploded, and he perished; superior condolence gifts were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Guangxu reign Zhang Zhidong summoned him to Hubei to oversee smokeless powder production; when the batch was complete the charge detonated and killed him, and the court granted special posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 華封，字祝三。

translations.literal: Huafeng, style name Zhusan.
translations.idiomatic: Huafeng, whose style name was Zhusan.

sentences.zh: 性敏，為父所愛，秘說精器多授之，以製造為治生。

translations.literal: Quick of mind, he was beloved by his father, who taught him many secret methods and refined instruments, and he made a living by manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and his father's favorite, he received most of the family's secret techniques and precision tools and earned his living through manufacturing.

sentences.zh: 建寅、華封並從父譯書行於世。

translations.literal: Jianyin and Huafeng both followed their father in translating books that circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyin and Huafeng both assisted their father in translations that were published widely.
